tutorial_example_entry.lesson_core_move: Simplify overlapping shifted-unit-step expressions by identifying their active time intervals and combining like signal segments into an equivalent compact expression.

blocks.text: Treat each shifted unit-step term as a gate that changes only when its argument crosses zero. In a sum of shifted steps, the switch times are the only time points where the expression can change value.

To simplify, list every switch time, sort them, and split the time axis into intervals between those times. On each interval, decide which step terms are active and add their coefficients; that sum is the active value for the interval.

blocks.latex: \text{Step boundaries: }t=1,2\;\Rightarrow\;\text{active interval values are computed piecewise}

blocks.text: For the base case, start with $x(t)=u(t)-u(t-1)+u(t-1)$. The boundaries are $t=0$ and $t=1$, so the interval values are $0$ for $t<0$, $1$ for $0\le t<1$, and $1$ for $t\ge 1$; that collapses to the compact form $u(t)$.

Use the same bookkeeping for expressions like $2u(t-1)-u(t-2)+3u(t-3)$: find the boundaries, combine the active coefficients interval by interval, and rewrite the result as a compact equivalent expression with no redundant overlap.

sections.section_title: Identifying Active Intervals in Shifted Unit Step Expressions

explanation_blocks.text: Read each shifted unit-step term as a gate that turns on at its own shift time and stays on to the right. For this expression, the shift times are the only boundaries that matter.

Sort those switch times and split the time axis into the four intervals $t<1$, $1\le t<3$, $3\le t<5$, and $t\ge 5$. On each interval, keep only the terms that are active there and add their coefficients.
So the active-interval map is $0$, then $3$, then $2$, then $4$. That is the output this step needs: the interval values written cleanly before any compact simplification.

The next step will reuse the same boundaries to combine these regions into a shorter equivalent step expression. For now, the key skill is identifying exactly which terms are active on each interval and summing them correctly.

example_content.example_prompt: Simplify $x(t)=u(t-2)+2u(t-4)-3u(t-6)$ and write a compact equivalent expression.

explanation_blocks.text: Each shifted unit-step term is constant on the intervals between its switch times, so the first step is to list those times and read the active value on each interval.
Split the time axis into $t<2$, $2\le t<4$, $4\le t<6$, and $t\ge 6$. On each interval, add the coefficients of the terms that are active there.

The interval values are $0$, then $1$, then $3$, then $0$. Read those changes at the switch times as the step coefficients: a jump of $1$ at $t=2$, a further jump of $2$ at $t=4$, and a drop of $3$ at $t=6$.

So the compact step expression is the same coefficient pattern written directly in shifted-step form. The active-interval map and the step sum agree on every interval, which is the bookkeeping rule this example is modeling.

example_content.example_prompt: Simplify $x(t)=(t-2)u(t-2)-(t-4)u(t-4)$ and express it as a compact piecewise form.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is that each shifted unit step turns a linear factor on only after its own switch time. Work interval by interval, and evaluate the slope only where the term is active.
Use the breakpoints to split the line into $t<2$, $2 \le t < 4$, and $t \ge 4$. In each region, keep only the active terms and simplify the linear expression that remains.

The overlap cancels the slopes after $t=4$, so the piecewise form above is already the compact result. If you want the same answer in step notation, one equivalent form is $x(t)=(t-2)(u(t-2)-u(t-4))+2u(t-4)$.

sections.section_title: Rewriting Redundant Step Terms into Compact Expressions

example_content.example_prompt: Rewrite $x(t)=u(t-2)-u(t-4)+u(t-4)-u(t-6)$ as a compact equivalent expression.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is the canceling pair in $x(t)=u(t-2)-u(t-4)+u(t-4)-u(t-6)$. Before removing it, split the signal at the breakpoints $t=2,4,6$ and evaluate each interval separately.
The middle two intervals match, so the boundary at $t=4$ is redundant. That means the pair $-u(t-4)+u(t-4)$ contributes nothing and can be removed.

One test point from each remaining interval confirms the equivalence: before $2$ the value is $0$, between $2$ and $6$ it is $1$, and after $6$ it returns to $0$. The compact form keeps only the net-effective switch events.

sections.section_title: Checking Simplified Step Expressions by Time Interval

example_content.example_prompt: Verify that $x(t)=2u(t-1)-u(t-3)-u(t-5)+u(t-4)$ is equivalent to $y(t)=2u(t-1)-u(t-3)+u(t-4)-u(t-5)$ by checking each active interval.

explanation_blocks.text: The cue is the ordered list of switch times $t=1,3,4,5$. Test one representative from each interval so you check the interior of every segment and the behavior at each boundary.
Every sample matches, so there is no interval mismatch and no boundary error. The candidate has the same active-value pattern as the original on all canonical intervals.
That is the verification rule to reuse: simplify first, then test one point from each canonical interval before you release the result.

question_entry.lesson_core_move: Simplify overlapping shifted-unit-step expressions by identifying their active time intervals and combining like signal segments into an equivalent compact expression.

sections.section_title: Identifying Active Intervals in Shifted Unit Step Expressions

prompt_blocks.text: Which interval-value expression is correct for the signal below?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The switch times are $1$, $4$, and $5$. That gives the active values $0$, $2$, $-1$, and $0$ on the intervals $t<1$, $1\le t<4$, $4\le t<5$, and $t\ge 5$.

prompt_blocks.text: Which interval-value expression is correct for the signal below?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The switch times are $2$, $5$, and $6$. So the active values are $0$, $3$, $1$, and $2$ on the four intervals, which is exactly choice A.

prompt_blocks.text: Simplify $x(t)=2u(t-1)-u(t-2)+u(t-4)-u(t-5)$ into an equivalent compact form.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The active values are $0$, then $2$, then $1$, then $2$, then $1$ on the intervals cut by the switch times $t=1,2,4,5$. That is exactly the coefficient pattern already written in the step sum, so no further reduction is needed.

prompt_blocks.text: Simplify $y(t)=u(t-1)-2u(t-3)+3u(t-5)-u(t-6)$ into an equivalent compact form.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The active values are $0$, then $1$, then $-1$, then $2$, then $1$ on the intervals cut by $t=1,3,5,6$. Those interval sums match the given step coefficients, so the compact equivalent form is the same step expression.

prompt_blocks.text: Which piecewise form is equivalent to $x(t)=(t-1)u(t-1)-2(t-3)u(t-3)+u(t-5)$?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The switch times are $1$, $3$, and $5$. Split the line at those points, keep only the active terms on each interval, and simplify the linear expression in each region.

prompt_blocks.text: Which piecewise form is equivalent to $y(t)=2(t-2)u(t-2)-(t-4)u(t-4)+(t-6)u(t-6)$?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The switch times are $2$, $4$, and $6$. On each interval, keep the active sloped terms only, combine them, and then simplify the result.

sections.section_title: Rewriting Redundant Step Terms into Compact Expressions

prompt_blocks.text: Rewrite $x(t)=u(t-1)-2u(t-3)+2u(t-3)-u(t-5)$ into the most compact equivalent step form.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The pair $-2u(t-3)+2u(t-3)$ cancels everywhere, so only the outer switches at $t=1$ and $t=5$ remain. The compact equivalent form is $u(t-1)-u(t-5)$.

prompt_blocks.text: Rewrite $x(t)=2u(t-2)-u(t-4)+u(t-4)-u(t-6)+u(t-6)-2u(t-8)$ into the most compact equivalent step form.

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The pairs at $t=4$ and $t=6$ cancel, so the only surviving switches are the jump of $2$ at $t=2$ and the drop of $2$ at $t=8$. The compact equivalent form is $2u(t-2)-2u(t-8)$.

sections.section_title: Checking Simplified Step Expressions by Time Interval

prompt_blocks.text: Which proposed simplification matches $x(t)=u(t-1)-u(t-2)+u(t-2)-u(t-4)$ on every canonical interval?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The switch times are $t=1,2,4$. Testing one representative from each interval gives $0$, $1$, $1$, and $0$ for both expressions.
Because the original and candidate agree on every canonical interval, the simplified form is equivalent.

prompt_blocks.text: Which proposed simplification matches $x(t)=2u(t-1)-u(t-3)-u(t-5)+u(t-4)$ on every canonical interval?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The switch times are $t=1,3,4,5$. Testing representatives $t=0$, $2$, $3.5$, $4.5$, and $6$ gives $0$, $2$, $1$, $2$, and $1$ for both expressions.
Because the values match on every canonical interval, the candidate passes the interval test.
